fossils.name: Ammonite
fossils.note: Coiled and forgiving. The whorls hold together.

fossils.name: Belemnite
fossils.note: Thin as a pencil. Treat it like one.

fossils.name: Ichthyosaur vertebrae
fossils.note: Scattered down the slab like dropped coins.

fossils.name: Ichthyosaur rib
fossils.note: A long curve. Easy to catch the end of.

fossils.name: Ichthyosaur paddle
fossils.note: Phalanges packed like cobbles.

fossils.name: Crinoid stem
fossils.note: A stack of tiny discs. Blow on it wrong and it is gravel.

fossils.name: Trilobite
fossils.note: Segmented. The grooves are shale, not bone.

fossils.name: Brachiopod
fossils.note: Small. Rarely alone.

fossils.name: Agnostid trilobite
fossils.note: Blind, tiny, everywhere.

fossils.name: Hyolith
fossils.note: A cone nobody agrees about.

fossils.name: Knightia
fossils.note: Ribs one cell wide. Breathe on them.

fossils.name: Fossil leaf
fossils.note: Thinner than the brush bristles.

fossils.name: Diplomystus
fossils.note: The big herring. Worth the patience.

fossils.name: Palm frond
fossils.note: Every blade is its own chance to ruin it.

fossils.name: Raptor claw
fossils.note: A crescent with an opinion.

fossils.name: T. rex tooth
fossils.note: Small, dense, and the reason you came.

fossils.name: T. rex rib
fossils.note: Runs corner to corner. Budget your daylight.

fossils.name: T. rex vertebra
fossils.note: Three fused drums of bone.

fossils.name: Triceratops horn
fossils.note: Enormous, and buried in nodules.

fossils.name: Gryphaea
fossils.note: Devil's toenail. Thick, curled, almost unbreakable.

fossils.name: Nautilus
fossils.note: Wider whorls than an ammonite, and fewer of them.

fossils.name: Plesiosaur tooth
fossils.note: Striated, slightly curved, and sharper than it has any right to be.

fossils.name: Dapedium
fossils.note: A dinner plate with fins. Scales like chainmail.

fossils.name: Elrathia
fossils.note: The trilobite everyone owns. Still a trilobite.

fossils.name: Eocrinoid
fossils.note: A cup on a stalk. The stalk is the part that goes.

fossils.name: Naraoia
fossils.note: Two shields and no shell between them. Rare and soft.

fossils.name: Priscacara
fossils.note: Deep-bodied perch. Spines along the back, every one countable.

fossils.name: Mioplosus
fossils.note: A predator, sometimes fossilised mid-meal.

fossils.name: Sycamore leaf
fossils.note: Veins like a river delta. They are also where it tears.

fossils.name: Crayfish
fossils.note: Claws out, as if it saw the lake turning.

fossils.name: Edmontosaurus tooth
fossils.note: One of a thousand in a jaw built for grinding.

fossils.name: Ankylosaur scute
fossils.note: Armour. It survived worse than your brush.

fossils.name: Hadrosaur rib
fossils.note: Long, curved, and thin in the middle where it always breaks.

fossils.name: Champsosaur vertebrae
fossils.note: A string of them, from something that outlived the asteroid.

fossils.name: Promicroceras
fossils.note: Small, tightly coiled, and everywhere once you see one.

fossils.name: Asteroceras
fossils.note: Ribbed like a cartwheel. The pride of a Dorset shelf.

fossils.name: Arnioceras
fossils.note: Fine ribs, closely set. They chip if you hurry.

fossils.name: Microderoceras
fossils.note: Spined whorls. The spines are the first thing to go.

fossils.name: Dactylioceras
fossils.note: Forked ribs, rope-like. Common and handsome.

fossils.name: Gastropod
fossils.note: A sea snail, thick-walled and patient.

fossils.name: Bivalve
fossils.note: Two halves, usually one left. Still counts.

fossils.name: Plesiosaur vertebrae
fossils.note: Spool-shaped, deeply dished at both ends.

fossils.name: Plesiosaur paddle
fossils.note: Finger bones fanned out like a dealt hand.

fossils.name: Ichthyosaur jaw
fossils.note: Teeth in a line down a snout built for speed.

fossils.name: Ichthyosaur skull
fossils.note: The eye socket is the size of your palm. Mind the ring of bone around it.

fossils.name: Pentacrinites
fossils.note: A crinoid still attached to its driftwood. Arms like frost.

fossils.name: Coprolite
fossils.note: Somebody's bad afternoon, preserved for two hundred million years.

fossils.name: Fish scales
fossils.note: Scattered diamonds of enamel. Easy to lose track of.

fossils.name: Belemnite cluster
fossils.note: A death assemblage. Several at once, all pointing the same way.

fossils.name: Pyritised ammonite
fossils.note: Fool's gold, and brittle with it.

fossils.name: Fossil driftwood
fossils.note: Bored through by shipworm before it sank.

fossils.name: Orthocone
fossils.note: A nautilus that never bothered coiling.

fossils.name: Asaphiscus
fossils.note: Broad-brimmed and placid. A good first trilobite.

fossils.name: Modocia
fossils.note: Small, neat, and easy to snap across the middle.

fossils.name: Peronopsis
fossils.note: Two plates and a hinge. Barely a fingernail.

fossils.name: Bathyuriscus
fossils.note: Long tail shield, fine segments. Count them if you dare.

fossils.name: Olenoides
fossils.note: Spines off every segment, and every one of them wants to break.

fossils.name: Ptychagnostus
fossils.note: A thumbnail with ambitions.

fossils.name: Lingulella
fossils.note: A brachiopod that still has living relatives. Unimpressed by extinction.

fossils.name: Wiwaxia
fossils.note: Scales and spines, and nobody agrees what it was.

fossils.name: Marrella
fossils.note: Lace-winged and impossible. The soft tissue is the whole value.

fossils.name: Hyolith cluster
fossils.note: Little cones, strewn like spilled cutlery.

fossils.name: Sponge
fossils.note: A glass basket. Treat it as one.

fossils.name: Algal mat
fossils.note: The bottom of the food chain, immortalised.

fossils.name: Eldonia
fossils.note: A disc with a gut coiled inside it. A jellyfish, more or less.

fossils.name: Anomalocaris claw
fossils.note: The apex predator of its world, and it fits in your hand.

fossils.name: Knightia shoal
fossils.note: A dozen at once, caught in the same bad minute.

fossils.name: Large Diplomystus
fossils.note: Upturned mouth, built to feed from below.

fossils.name: Phareodus
fossils.note: Teeth and a sail of a dorsal fin. A real predator.

fossils.name: Amphiplaga
fossils.note: A trout-perch, and rarer than it looks.

fossils.name: Notogoneus
fossils.note: Long and bottom-feeding. Mostly found in pieces.

fossils.name: Gar scales
fossils.note: Enamelled diamonds, hard as tooth.

fossils.name: Stingray
fossils.note: Heraldica. The whole disc, and the tail if you are lucky.

fossils.name: Fossil insect
fossils.note: Wings like cellophane. One careless pass and it is dust.

fossils.name: Feather
fossils.note: Barbs still separate. The most fragile thing in the ground.

fossils.name: Willow leaf
fossils.note: Long and narrow, veins running the length of it.

fossils.name: Maple leaf
fossils.note: Lobed and symmetrical. Autumn, fifty million years ago.

fossils.name: Fern frond
fossils.note: Pinnae down both sides. Every one of them separate.

fossils.name: Fossil flower
fossils.note: Petals. Actual petals. Nobody will believe you.

fossils.name: Turtle carapace
fossils.note: Plates fused into a dome. Solid, for once.

fossils.name: Crocodilian tooth
fossils.note: Conical, striated, and shed by the hundred.

fossils.name: Tyrannosaur claw
fossils.note: Blunt for a theropod. It did not need to be sharp.

fossils.name: Tyrannosaur skull fragment
fossils.note: Thick, pitted bone. Part of something enormous.

fossils.name: Triceratops frill
fossils.note: A shield of bone with a scalloped edge.

fossils.name: Triceratops tooth
fossils.note: A shearing tooth from a battery of hundreds.

fossils.name: Hadrosaur tooth battery
fossils.note: Teeth stacked like coins in a roll. Lose one and the row is wrong.

fossils.name: Ankylosaur spike
fossils.note: Armour that fought back.

fossils.name: Pachycephalosaur dome
fossils.note: Ten inches of solid skull. Built for arguments.

fossils.name: Dromaeosaur tooth
fossils.note: Serrated on the back edge. Check it with a thumbnail, gently.

fossils.name: Mosasaur tooth
fossils.note: From the inland sea that cut the continent in half.

fossils.name: Champsosaur jaw
fossils.note: Needle teeth in a gharial's snout.

fossils.name: Turtle scute
fossils.note: One plate of a shell that saw the asteroid.

fossils.name: Crocodilian osteoderm
fossils.note: Pitted armour from a back that lay in the shallows.

fossils.name: Mammal jaw
fossils.note: Smaller than your thumb, and worth more than the tyrannosaur.

fossils.name: Eggshell fragments
fossils.note: Curved shards with a pore pattern. Jigsaw with no picture.

fossils.name: Petrified wood
fossils.note: Agatised rings. Harder than the rock around it.

fossils.name: Sphenodiscus
fossils.note: A late ammonite, from the last of them.

fossils.name: Magnolia leaf
fossils.note: Flowering plants, newly arrived and already everywhere.

fossils.name: Theropod vertebrae
fossils.note: Hollow-chambered and lighter than it should be.

fossils.name: Tyrannosaurus skull
fossils.note: The whole head. You will not finish it today, and you will try.

fossils.name: Tyrannosaurus tail
fossils.note: Vertebra after vertebra, thinning to nothing. Count them as they come up.

fossils.name: Tyrannosaurus foot
fossils.note: Three toes and a hallux. Each claw the size of your hand.

fossils.name: Dromaeosaur foot
fossils.note: The killing claw is held off the ground. It is also the first thing to snap.

fossils.name: Triceratops skull
fossils.note: Beak, horn cores and a frill that will not fit on the slab.

fossils.name: Hadrosaur ribcage
fossils.note: A ladder of ribs. Lose one and everybody can tell.

fossils.name: Ankylosaur skull
fossils.note: Built like a kerbstone. One of the few things here you cannot easily ruin.

fossils.name: Pterosaur wing
fossils.note: One finger longer than the rest of the animal, and a membrane like tissue paper.

fossils.name: Mosasaur skull
fossils.note: Teeth in the roof of its mouth as well. Nothing it bit got away.

fossils.name: Crocodilian skull
fossils.note: Flat, long, and grinning. It has not changed much since.

fossils.name: Ichthyosaur tail
fossils.note: It bends down at the end, where the fin was.

fossils.name: Plesiosaur ribcage
fossils.note: Barrel-chested. Gastroliths sometimes still inside.

fossils.name: Plesiosaur skull
fossils.note: Small for the animal, and all of it teeth.

fossils.name: Pterodactylus wing
fossils.note: The first one ever found was called a sea-bird. They were not even close.

fossils.name: Dimorphodon skull
fossils.note: A puffin's head on a flying lizard. Hollow everywhere.

fossils.name: Fossil bird
fossils.note: Hollow bones, and a wishbone you can see. Breathe on it wrong and it is gone.

fossils.name: Fossil bat
fossils.note: Fingers as wing struts, exactly like the pterosaurs, fifty million years later.

fossils.name: Anomalocaris, whole
fossils.note: Swimming flaps down both sides. The best thing in the shale, and the softest.

fossils.name: Tyrannosaurus, articulated
fossils.note: Spine, ribs, an arm, and the head still attached. Nobody finds these.

fossils.name: Dromaeosaur, articulated
fossils.note: Curled where it died. Every bone of it thinner than your brush.

fossils.name: Plesiosaur, articulated
fossils.note: Mary Anning found one at twelve. You have until sundown.

sites.name: Charmouth, Dorset
sites.twist: Blue Lias, three honest layers. Nothing is out to get you here.

sites.name: Wheeler Shale, Utah
sites.twist: Shale splits thin. Less to brush through, several specimens per slab.

sites.name: Green River, Wyoming
sites.twist: Lake shale. The fish are paper and crack a third more readily, but a whole one is worth half again as much.

sites.name: Hell Creek, Montana
sites.twist: Big bones, and three more nodules of ironstone sat on top of them.

sites.name: Night dig
sites.twist: Headlamp only. Twelve seconds less daylight, and half again on everything you bag.

perk.label: Apex predator — Hell Creek fossils pay +15%
Sea dragon — every slab gets 5 more seconds of daylight

tools.name: Brush
tools.blurb: The one you already own. Honest, middling, forgiving enough.

tools.name: Fine brush
tools.blurb: Narrow and slow. Bone survives things it has no right to.

tools.name: Air blower
tools.blurb: Clears a hand's width at a time. Will also ruin a Knightia instantly.

tools.name: Dental pick
tools.blurb: Ironstone nodules give up at a third of the usual fight.

tools.name: X-ray goggles
tools.blurb: Three seconds of knowing exactly where not to rush.

tools.name: Headlamp
tools.blurb: Ten more seconds of daylight. The sun does not know about this.

tools.name: Sieve
tools.blurb: Gems pay double. It does nothing at all for the fossil.

charms.name: Authentic damage
charms.blurb: Cracked bone counts half intact. Collectors like a little history.

charms.name: Steady hands
charms.blurb: Every tool's safe speed, a quarter higher.

charms.name: Night owl
charms.blurb: Fifteen more seconds. A tenth less money. Worth it more often than not.

charms.name: Collector's eye
charms.blurb: You know what it is at a tenth exposed.

charms.name: Rush job
charms.blurb: Bag with twenty seconds to spare and he pays forty percent over.

charms.name: Rock hound
charms.blurb: Eight dollars for every nodule you clear out entirely.

charms.name: Compound interest
charms.blurb: Two percent more on everything, for each charm you are carrying.

charms.name: Cretaceous permit
charms.blurb: Every third slab comes out of Hell Creek, wherever you happen to be.

charms.name: Gem cradle
charms.blurb: Gems pay half again. Stacks with a sieve, cheerfully.

charms.name: Long shadows
charms.blurb: Eight more seconds of usable light.

charms.name: Provenance papers
charms.blurb: Ten percent more on everything. Nobody asks where they came from.

charms.name: Union card
charms.blurb: Six dollars a nodule, and the rock itself argues less.

charms.name: Patient hand
charms.blurb: Your hand steadies as the week goes on. Five percent per day survived.

charms.name: Collector's loupe
charms.blurb: Identified at a twentieth exposed, and worth fifteen percent more.

charms.name: Steady lamp
charms.blurb: Twenty more seconds, and a tenth fewer cracks.

charms.name: Diamond sieve
charms.blurb: Gems pay treble. The Collector pretends not to notice.

achievements.name: Not a mark on it
achievements.blurb: Bag a slab fully exposed with nothing cracked.

achievements.name: Keeping him sweet
achievements.blurb: Pay three installments in a row.

achievements.name: Almost respectable
achievements.blurb: Pay ten installments in a row.

personalMilestones.name: First thousand
personalMilestones.beat: He writes it down without looking up.

personalMilestones.name: Known at the gate
personalMilestones.beat: The foreman starts using your name.

personalMilestones.name: Worth the daylight
personalMilestones.beat: Somebody holds the lamp a little longer for you.

personalMilestones.name: Trusted with the good stock
personalMilestones.beat: The vault inventory lands on your side of the desk.

personalMilestones.name: Half a million of his money
personalMilestones.beat: He has stopped pretending this is about the money.

personalMilestones.name: Named in the Book
personalMilestones.beat: Your name, in his hand, on the first page.

upgrades.name: Steady grip
upgrades.blurb: Years of this. Your hand knows the weight now.

upgrades.name: A better lamp
upgrades.blurb: Not a luxury. The last hour of a day is worth two of the first.

upgrades.name: Soft bristles
upgrades.blurb: He laughed at the price. He stopped laughing at the ribs.

upgrades.name: A second pocket
upgrades.blurb: Room for one more charm, and the nerve to use it.

upgrades.name: Wheeler's patience
upgrades.blurb: He will wait a day longer. He will not say why.

upgrades.name: A practised eye
upgrades.blurb: You see the shape under the sandstone before the sandstone knows.

buyers.name: Wheeler
buyers.blurb: Takes it off your hands and marks the ledger. Asks nothing, ever.

buyers.name: The Munich dealer
buyers.blurb: Pays properly. The paperwork is always being seen to.

buyers.name: A man at the docks
buyers.blurb: Twice the money, cash, and it never happened. Nothing reaches the crew.

buyers.name: County museum
buyers.blurb: Half what it is worth, and your name back under glass.
